title: Song of the Good Man (Annotated)
author: Lü Xinwu
excerpt: Editor's note: The Master (Lü Xinwu) was named Kun, style name Shujian, a native of Ningling, a jinshi of the Jiajing reign of the Ming dynasty, who rose to the office of Junior Minister of Justice.

inline.s: Editor's note: The Master
(Lü Xinwu)
was named Kun, style name Shujian, a native of Ningling, and a jinshi of the Jiajing reign of the Ming dynasty, who rose to the office of Junior Minister of Justice
(that is, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice)

Hongmou's note: Everyone knows to love and admire the good person, yet in his own thoughts and conduct he is sometimes close to being not good! Now they are set out one by one. Who is a good person and who is a not-good person can be seen in each case as it arises. Those who have aspiration may take this as a mirror for examining themselves.

Vernacular translation: Everyone knows to love and admire the good person, and yet a person's own thoughts and conduct are sometimes close to being not good! Now the Song of the Good Man sets out, one by one, what a good person is and what a not-good person is. How to be a good person and how to be a not-good person can be seen at a clear glance from the various matters related in the song. Those resolved to become good persons may take it as a mirror for self-examination.
All things heaven and earth bring forth, yet of all things man is the most worthy. Among the human race there are good persons, who rise above the common run.
[Among the human race there are good persons, who rise above the common run] The good person among the race of mankind is one who stands out above the rest of men.
The good man first keeps faith and trust; the good man honors filial piety and brotherly love. The good man knows shame and integrity; the good man guards the rites and righteousness.

[Filial piety and brotherly love (xiào tì)] also written “filial respect and fraternal love”: being filial to one's parents and respectful to one's elder brothers. [tì] To honor and love one's elder brother.
The good man does not give loose to wine; the good man does not dote on courtesans. The good man does not gamble away his money; the good man does not act on mere temper.
[Acting on mere temper (shàng qì)] Giving way to one's passions and acting upon them.
The good man does not rely on his wealth; the good man does not lean on his power. The good man does not owe the grain-tax; the good man does not encroach on others' land.

[Does not owe the grain-tax] Does not owe the grain-tribute paid to the government. [Official grain] The tax-grain delivered to the authorities in former times. [Does not encroach on land] Does not seize the fields of others.
The good man does not incite mischief; the good man does not envy. The good man does not lie; the good man does not mock and tease.
[Incite mischief (jiào suō)] To egg on and direct (others to do wrong). [Mock and tease (xuè xì)] To jest and play tricks.
The good man utters no words of estrangement; the good man does not speak against others. The good man has no evil friends; the good man frequents no wild gatherings.
[Words of estrangement] also written “words of discord (jiàn yán)”: words that sow ill will among others. [Evil friends] Bad companions. [Wild gatherings] Dissolute, disorderly meetings.
The good man is not rude and coarse; the good man is not insolent and perverse. The good man is not lazy; the good man does not spend extravagantly.
[Rude and coarse (cūn yě)] Rough and reckless. [Insolent and perverse (kuáng bèi)] Arrogant and contrary to reason. [Spend extravagantly] To squander and waste.
The good man is not frivolous; the good man is not gaudy. The good man is not unkempt; the good man is not sly and strange.
[Sly and strange (qiāo xī)] Crafty and devious.
The good man is not tyrannical and fierce; the good man is not benighted and dull. The good man rescues those in distress; the good man bestows favors.
[Tyrannical and fierce (qiáng liáng)] Violent and overbearing. [Benighted and dull (àn mèi)] Stupid and ignorant.
The good man does what is convenient and kind; the good man yields the advantage to others. The wicked man reviles the good man; the good man gives no reply.
The wicked man strikes the good man; the good man only steps aside. Whether one be high or low, the good man offends none.
In matters great and small, the good man accords with the principle of heaven. If the rich man becomes a good man, his hidden merit reaches to later generations.

[Hidden merit (yīn gōng)] Good deeds done in this world by which merit is credited in the unseen realm. [Hidden merit reaches to later generations] The blessing of hidden merit extends to the descendants.
If the noble man becomes a good man, the townsfolk do not curse him. If the poor man becomes a good man, what need to speak of a thousand qing of land!

[Townsfolk (xiāng dǎng)] The people of one's home countryside. [Curse (lì)] To revile. [If the poor man becomes a good man, what need to speak of a thousand qing of land] The benefit of a poor man's becoming a good man far surpasses the owning of a thousand qing of fields.
If the lowly man becomes a good man, he outranks the pride of princes and marquises. If the young man becomes a good man, his virtue and renown equal those of his elders.
[If the lowly man becomes a good man, he outranks the pride of princes and marquises] A lowly man becoming a good man is far more honorable than princes and marquises.
If the old man becomes a good man, he covers over all the sins of his whole life. If the weak man becomes a good man, the mighty man is put to shame.
If the wicked man becomes a good man, his fame is multiplied a thousandfold. The good man is a treasure of his village and land; the good man is an auspice of his family and country.
[The good man is an auspice of his family and country] The good man is the fortune-bringing sign (the auspicious omen) of the family and the state.
The good man moves ghosts and spirits; the good man inspires heaven and earth. He does not live a human life in vain; he speaks out the righteous breath on heaven's behalf.

[The good man moves ghosts and spirits, the good man inspires heaven and earth] The good man moves ghosts and spirits; the good man moves heaven and earth. [Speaks out on heaven's behalf] The principle of heaven is often misconstrued and defiled by people; the good man, by his own example, confirms it, clarifies it, and spreads it abroad.
Alas! A hundred years pass and never return; do not become a wicked man and befoul the world.
[Befoul the world] To pollute the world. [Befoul (wò)] To dirty, to stain.
